title: Market Insights
text:
This page summarizes several characteristics of the housing price index dataset.
The goal is to move beyond a single chart and examine the size, time period, and variation represented in the data.






186,011
Total observations.




472
Unique locations.




1975
Earliest year.




2026
Latest year.


















The range measures the difference between the highest and lowest index value recorded within each year.












A larger range means that the index values represented in the data were more spread out within that year.
The range does not tell us why the differences occurred. It simply provides a way to describe variation in the observations.



Summary statistics can help us identify patterns that are not immediately obvious from individual observations.
Use Data Explorer next to examine the underlying rows that produce these summaries.

title: About
text:
Hi! My name is Brianna Eubank, and I am a student-athlete at New College of Florida in Sarasota, Florida.
This project was created as a data science project to explore housing price index data, practice data visualization, and communicate findings through an interactive website.




Name: Brianna Eubank
Email: b.eubank28@ncf.edu
GitHub: Brianna22222
Repository: Canadian-housing-price-index
College: New College of Florida




This project uses the FHFA House Price Index (HPI) dataset published by the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA).
The FHFA HPI is a collection of publicly available house price indexes that measures changes in single-family home values across the United States. The dataset includes information for different geographic levels, including the United States, Census Divisions, states, metropolitan areas, counties, and other areas. The project uses variables such as geographic location, year, period, index type, and housing price index values to examine patterns over time. :contentReferenceoaicite:2



The analysis in this website focuses on describing patterns found in the data.
The project examines:

Housing price index changes over time
Differences between geographic regions
Annual averages
Variation within years
The structure of the underlying dataset

The visualizations are created using R, ggplot2, tidyverse, and Quarto.





Introduces the project and provides an overview of the housing price index.



Examines how the housing price index changes over time.



Compares housing price index patterns across selected U.S. Census Divisions.



Uses several visualizations to communicate patterns found in the data.



Provides summary statistics and examines variation in the dataset.



Provides a closer look at the underlying observations and variables.



Provides information about the project, creator, and data source.




Federal Housing Finance Agency — FHFA House Price Index
The official FHFA HPI dataset page provides access to the master data, monthly data, quarterly data, annual data, and documentation. :contentReferenceoaicite:3
Source: FHFA House Price Index®

title: Housing Stories
text:
Data becomes more useful when we can turn numbers into questions and observations.
This page presents several stories that can be explored using the housing price index data.


The first story is about long-term change.
The annual average housing price index provides a simple way to see how index values move across the years.











The chart shows the broad movement of the index across the time period represented in the dataset.
Rather than focusing on a single month or location, the annual average provides a high-level view of the data.





The second story is about geography.
Housing price index values can vary between locations, meaning that looking only at an overall average may not show the full picture.
The Regional Comparisons page examines this idea by comparing U.S. Census Divisions.


If two regions experience the same general direction of change, do they necessarily experience the same magnitude of change?
The regional chart allows us to investigate that question.





The third story is about how the same dataset can answer different questions.
We can use the data to examine:

Change over time
Differences between locations
The number of observations available
Variation within a year
Differences between seasonally adjusted and non-seasonally adjusted values

This is why the project includes multiple pages rather than relying on a single visualization.




Use the other pages to continue exploring:
Housing Trends
Look at long-term changes.
Regional Comparisons
Compare geographic patterns.
Market Insights
Examine summary measurements and variation.
Data Explorer
Look directly at the underlying observations.
The goal is not just to look at a graph, but to use the data to ask better questions.

title: U.S. Housing Price Index
text:
Welcome to my Housing Price Index project. This website explores how housing price index values have changed over time and how patterns differ across geographic regions in the United States.
The project uses data from the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) House Price Index to examine long-term housing market patterns.






186,011
Housing price index observations in the dataset.




472
Geographic locations represented.




1975
Beginning of the dataset’s time period.




2026
Latest year represented in the dataset.






The chart below summarizes the annual average housing price index across the observations in the dataset.












A housing price index provides a way to examine changes in home prices over time. Instead of focusing on the price of one individual home, an index summarizes price movement across a group of properties.
The FHFA House Price Index is based on repeat transactions and refinancings involving single-family properties with mortgages purchased or securitized by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. :contentReferenceoaicite:1



Use the navigation bar to explore different parts of the analysis.

Housing Trends — examine changes in the index over time.
Regional Comparisons — compare patterns across U.S. Census Divisions.
Housing Stories — explore several patterns found in the data.
Market Insights — examine summary measurements and variation.
Data Explorer — look more closely at the underlying observations.
About — learn about the project, creator, and data source.

title: Housing Price Index Overview
text:
Welcome to the Housing Price Index project. This homepage visualizes housing price index changes across U.S. states, metropolitan areas, and other geographic regions over time.
#| echo: false #| message: false #| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv(“data/hpi_master.csv”, show_col_types = FALSE)
annual <- df |> group_by(yr) |> summarize( average_index = mean(index_nsa, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = “drop” )
ggplot() + geom_point( data = df, aes(x = yr, y = index_nsa), alpha = 0.08, size = 0.7, color = “#2563eb” ) + geom_line( data = annual, aes(x = yr, y = average_index), linewidth = 1.2, color = “#dc2626” ) + theme_minimal() + labs( title = “U.S. House Price Index Trends (1975–Present)”, subtitle = “Individual observations with annual averages shown as a line”, x = “Year”, y = “House Price Index” )

title: Regional Comparisons
text:
Housing markets can behave differently across geographic areas. This page compares selected U.S. Census Divisions using the housing price index.
For this comparison, the data is filtered to traditional, purchase-only, monthly observations at the U.S. and Census Division level.


The chart compares annual average index values across six locations represented in the filtered dataset.












A national or overall average can hide differences between geographic areas.
Comparing regions allows us to see whether different locations follow similar or different patterns over time.




Do the regions follow similar patterns?
Are some regions more variable than others?
Are there periods when regional differences become larger?
Does the overall pattern look similar to the national trend?

The Housing Stories page uses these ideas to tell several data-based stories.

title: Housing Trends
text:
How has the housing price index changed over the years?
This page focuses on the overall movement of housing price index values through time.


The annual average provides a simplified view of the overall pattern in the dataset.












The mean and median provide two different summaries of the observations.












Looking at the two summaries helps us examine whether the overall pattern is similar when using the mean and median.
The index is a relative measure, so the focus of this project is on changes and patterns over time, rather than interpreting the index as a dollar price.




How does the index change over time?
Are there periods with larger changes?
Do the mean and median show similar patterns?
How might the pattern differ between geographic regions?

Continue to Regional Comparisons to investigate geographic differences.
